concepts.preferred_label: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
concepts.why: The patient was diagnosed with pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect and a patent ductus arteriosus, which is a congenital heart defect.
The patient was diagnosed with immune thrombocytopenia based on a low platelet count and a prolonged platelet aggregation time.
The patient presented with cyanosis, which is a condition characterized by a bluish discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes due to low oxygen saturation.
The patient was diagnosed with a patent ductus arteriosus, which is a congenital heart defect.
The patient was diagnosed with a ventricular septal defect, which is a congenital heart defect.
The patient presented with respiratory distress, which is a condition characterized by difficulty breathing.
The patient presented with thrombocytopenia, which is a condition characterized by a low platelet count.
The patient presented with anemia, which is a condition characterized by a low red blood cell count or hemoglobin level.
